To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the following mass patterns are disfavored: m1 < m2 < m3 < m4, m1 < m3 < 1 m4, m2 < m4 < 1 m3 and m2 < 1 m1 < m4, if neutrinos turn out to be Majorana.
the four neutrino scheme can be reduced to three allowed mass patterns and that the most likely one is the so-called normal hierarchy, with a 2σ lower bound on the neutrino mass of ∼ 0.05
the four neutrino scheme is not in conflict with the ββ0 ν decay rate, but that some of the mass patterns are ruled out by this constraint.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of neutrino mass eigenstates and the determination of the number of light neutrinos.
the question of how many neutrinos exist and what their masses and mixing angles are.
the question: what can be learned about the neutrino sector from neutrinoless ββ decay?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inverted mass hierarchy is favored by all the data, and the large mixing angle (LMA) MSW solution for solar neutrinos is the only viable solution.
the most favored pattern is that of the inverted mass hierarchy, with the heaviest neutrino mass of order a few eV, and the other three masses below 0.1 eV.

the most likely four neutrino mass pattern (with a normal mass hierarchy, a large θ13, a large δ and a large θ23, but with the LSND result disfavored) is still allowed by the existing experimental data, but it would be very desirable to have an independent experimental verification of the neutrino oscillation results from the LSND and MiniBooNE experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two lowest mass patterns, which are the most favored by the oscillation data, are also favored by the upper bound on ββ0ν, but that the other four mass patterns are disfavored.
the most favored mass pattern is the one with the smallest neutrino mass difference Δm21, while a second one is the most favored among those with a larger Δm21.
the four neutrino mass pattern with m1 < m2 < m3 < m4 is disfavored by ββ0ν data, whereas all other patterns remain viable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of a signal from ββ0ν, the LSND result can be reconciled only with a small neutrino mass scale and with a very large mixing angle.

a four neutrino mass spectrum with normal mass ordering and the largest mass splitting between the lightest and the heaviest neutrinos (the so-called “inverted mass ordering”) is the most favored one, if the neutrino masses are assumed to be degenerate.
the LSND data, which are currently not in agreement with the other neutrino oscillation experiments, are still compatible with the existence of a Majorana neutrino mass scale in the 0.1-1 eV range.
